definition: GDP per capita is a country's total economic output in a year divided by its population. It is the standard measure for comparing average income levels between countries.

prose: The top of the GDP per capita table is unusually stable. Five of {{firstYear}}'s top ten countries still rank in {{latestYear}}'s top ten: {{overlapList}}. Where movement occurs, it concentrates in a small number of countries. Late industrialisers that started low have climbed, and a handful of countries that began reporting after {{firstYear}} have entered near the top.

faq.q: Which country has climbed the rankings most since {{firstYear}}?
faq.a: Among {{latestYear}}'s top ten, {{climberName}} recorded the largest climb, rising from {{climberRankFirstYearOrd}} in {{firstYear}} to {{climberLatestRankOrd}} in {{latestYear}}. Across every country with reported data, several outside the top ten show larger absolute movements; the downloadable CSV includes the complete rank history.

methodology: Figures are GDP per capita in current US dollars as published in the {{sourceLink}} (indicator NY.GDP.PCAP.CD), retrieved {{retrievedAtHuman}}. Rankings are computed among all countries with reported data for each year; countries with no reported value in a given year are excluded from that year's ranking. Because values are nominal, changes over time reflect both real growth and US-dollar inflation; within-year rankings are unaffected. Trajectory sparklines index each country's series to its own {{firstYear}}–{{latestYear}} range and are not comparable in level across rows.
